transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm just... I don't feel like myself anymore. I guess that's why I'm here. I barely talk to anyone these days. I just sort of... go flat and quiet. And work... I'm a janitor, and lately, just getting started on my cleaning route feels like trying to push a loaded cart uphill. I just don't have it in me.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Well, yeah, I have. Usually when I’m mopping after hours. I'll hear this man’s voice... he'll say my name, or sometimes he tells me I’ve missed a spot. It sounds completely real, clear as if he’s standing right by the stairwell. But when I look over, there's nobody there.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric for days at a time?

No, not really. I don't think I've ever felt like that. Honestly, it's mostly just the opposite. I'm usually just tired and dragging myself around. I definitely haven't had any days where I'm full of energy or overly happy.
Do you ever hear that man’s voice when your mood is not low?

Yeah, actually I do. There was a... a stretch of several weeks a while back when my mood had lifted some. I was getting through my meals and my work a little better, not feeling quite so heavy. But even then, I still heard my name being called in the stairwell. And... I stayed convinced that the hallway cameras were being used to track me, even when I wasn't feeling so down.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, definitely. It's been a lot longer than two weeks, to be honest. Really, for most of the time since the move, that... that sadness has just been there. Along with the low energy, feeling guilty, and just losing interest in pretty much everything. 

It's like it is always running in the background. Even on the days when hearing that man's voice or worrying about the cameras is the main thing on my mind... that heavy, sad feeling is still right there underneath it all.
Was there ever a time when the voice and the feeling that the cameras were tracking you lasted for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago... there was that stretch of several weeks where my mood had lifted. I wasn't feeling depressed during that time, and I was getting through my meals and my cleaning work at the building a lot better. But even for those couple of weeks when my mood was okay, I still heard my name in the stairwell, and I stayed convinced that the hallway cameras were tracking me.
Can you tell me what makes you believe the hallway cameras are tracking you?

Well, I just... I get stuck on this idea that the new landlord and a couple of people in my new building are keeping tabs on me. It feels like they're using those hallway cameras to watch me and then passing messages about me behind my back. Other folks have told me that those cameras are just for the front door, you know, just for basic security. But... I don't know, I just can't shake the feeling that they're tracking what I do.
When you talk, do people ever tell you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that your speech seems jumbled?

Yeah, I've noticed that happening, and people have pointed it out. Sometimes my supervisor will ask me a really simple question, like... just asking which floors I've finished cleaning. And instead of just telling him, I start talking about... I don't know, the old bus route I used to take, or the garden plot, or the church basement. 

I can hear myself doing it while I'm talking. I realize I'm not getting back to the answer he actually asked for, but the thoughts just kind of come out jumbled like that.
Even when you are not feeling depressed, do you still tend to stay flat and talk very little?

Yeah, I do. That's actually a big part of what brought me in, really. I just don't feel like myself anymore. Even when I'm not feeling down, I barely talk to people. I just go flat and quiet. And trying to get things done... even getting started on my cleaning route feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill.
Over the whole time you've been having these problems, has depression been there for most of that time?

Yeah, I'd say so. Really, for most of the time since the move, it's been there. The sadness, the low energy... feeling guilty and just losing interest in everything... it's all just kind of sat there in the background. Even on the days when the voices or my worries about those cameras are the main thing on my mind, that down feeling is still right there underneath it all.
